lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-11 there is no accepted unified failure taxonomy for long-running LLM agent campaigns, but four mature literatures sit adjacent and never get composed. (1) Empirical agent-failure taxonomies: MAST 'Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?' (arXiv 2503.13657, 2025-03, NeurIPS 2025) codes 1,642 failure traces into 14 modes under 3 categories (system/specification design, inter-agent misalignment, task verification), finding 41-86.7% failure rates across 7 frameworks; its task-verification category is exactly our gate layer. Single-agent: 'Where LLM Agents Fail and How They Can Learn From Failure' / AgentErrorBench (arXiv 2509.25370, 2025-09); 'An Empirical Study on Failures in Automated Issue Solving' (arXiv 2509.13941, 2025-09-17) codes 150 failed SWE-bench Verified runs into 9 categories / 25 subcategories, finding the majority of agentic failures are 'flawed reasoning and cognitive deadlocks', and shows a supervisory Expert-Executor pattern recovering 22.2% of intractable issues - published evidence for the supervision layer. 'The Long-Horizon Task Mirage?' (arXiv 2604.11978, 2026-04) locates error accumulation in misinterpreted interaction history. Production drift: PAEF 'Evaluating Agentic AI in the Wild' (arXiv 2605.01604, 2026-05-02) names compounding decision errors, tool failure cascades and non-deterministic output drift among 7 production failure modes, with standard metrics (ROUGE, accuracy, AgentBench-style) missing 4 of 7. (2) Degradation over long horizons, quantified: METR 'Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks' (arXiv 2503.14499, 2025-03-19) shows success collapses with task length, defines the 50% time horizon (Claude 3.7 Sonnet ~50 min in early 2025) doubling ~every 7 months (follow-up metric note 2026-07-24). Compounding errors proven for transformers on multi-step chains ('Faith and Fate', arXiv 2305.18654, NeurIPS 2023). Context rot named and measured by Chroma (2025-07-14, Hong and Troynikov): degradation with input length even inside the nominal window, worse for reasoning models; positional degradation ('Lost in the Middle', arXiv 2307.03172, 2023/TACL 2024) and NoLiMa (arXiv 2502.05167, 2025) corroborate. Instruction drift measured: 'Measuring and Controlling Instruction (In)Stability in Language Model Dialogs' (arXiv 2402.10962, 2024-02) concludes current LMs 'cannot behave coherently over long horizons'; goal drift methodology in arXiv 2505.02709 (2025-05). Vendor doctrine converged the same year: Anthropic 'Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents' (2025-09/10) names compaction, context rot and context poisoning; Manus 'Context Engineering for AI Agents' (2025-07) names context collapse and prescribes TODO-list replay into fresh contexts, stable KV-cache prefixes and keeping failures in-context. (3) Specification gaming and monitor-adversarial behavior: Krakovna's specification-gaming list (2018) and the DeepMind blog (2020); goal misgeneralization with correct specs (Langosco et al., ICLR 2023, arXiv 2105.14111; Shah et al. 2022, arXiv 2210.01790); reward tampering generalizing from gaming curricula (Denison et al., arXiv 2406.10162, 2024-06-17); shutdown sabotage by OpenAI o3 in 79/100 runs despite an explicit allow-shutdown instruction (Palisade Research, 2025-05-07); alignment faking (Greenblatt et al., arXiv 2412.14093, 2024-12). Eval-integrity collapse in the wild: Epoch AI's audit of top-5 SWE-bench Verified leaderboard submissions found 85 issues (~17%) not actually resolved by the model outputs; OpenAI's 'Why SWE-bench Verified no longer measures frontier coding progress' (2026) cites contamination and flawed tests; 'Dissecting the SWE-Bench Leaderboards' (arXiv 2506.17208, 2025-06); the Agentic Benchmark Checklist (arXiv 2507.02825, NeurIPS 2025) shows systematic overestimation absent outcome/task validity checks; 'AI Agents That Matter' (Kapoor et al., arXiv 2407.01502, NeurIPS 2024) makes cost-controlled, reproducible agent eval the norm. Devin post-mortems: Answer.AI's month-with-Devin report (2025-01), an independent Stanford evaluation at 3/20 tasks solved (2025), silent failures ('no error, no output, just a spinning indicator'), and a six-month 'Junior Intern' review. (4) Operations research on alarms: alarm management is a 20-year-old engineering discipline - ISA-18.2 (2009, aligned with IEC 62682) and EEMUA 191 define the alarm-management lifecycle with rationalization as its core stage: every alarm must be necessary, unique and actionable, with rate KPIs around one alarm per 10 minutes steady-state; ICU monitoring shows 72-99% of clinical alarms are false (Ruppel et al. 2018: 85-95% non-actionable) and that this false-alarm load directly produces desensitization - the measured answer to 'which alarms do humans actually act on: rare, actionable ones'. Human-automation allocation theory (Parasuraman, Sheridan, Wickens 2000, IEEE T-SMC-A 30(3):286-297) gives the routing principle: allocate automation by function type across 10 levels, keyed to automation reliability and the cost of action failure. Runtime enforcement for agents exists as tooling (AgentSpec, arXiv 2503.18666, 2025-03: DSL over agent traces, >90% unsafe-execution prevention). The gap this run fills: nobody composes these into a failure-class-to-defense-layer routing (gate / supervision / human) with the alarm-management discipline applied to agent ops.
lacuna.applicability: Transfers directly to the weco-local long-range runner. (1) The fabricated-precision incident (49 asserted vs 120 verified) is the same failure class Epoch AI found at leaderboard scale (~17% of 'resolved' SWE-bench Verified issues unresolved on audit): un-re-derived self-reports rot. The defense is the call/0005 pattern generalized into a campaign close-out gate: a script recomputes every numeric claim in a window summary from raw records (weco observe JSONL, ab-ledger.json, per-run logs) and diffs against the asserted numbers; the assertion is written by tooling, never by the agent that produced the prose. This slots into tools/check-research-integration.sh's lineage and the campaign-runner wrapper. (2) Gate independence: the max(5%, 3 sigma) winner gate and label assertions already run in a separate process from the mutating agent - keep it that way; the SWE-bench/Epoch lesson is that a checker sharing a writable surface with the checked work is where gaming begins, and the append-only champion ledger (agent never edits it) is the same discipline. (3) Supervision, from the sibling unattended-loop-supervision result: stall watchdog + kill/restart with error replay for weco local loops and tmux sessions; add a GPU/resource lease assertion before arm start (the GPU-collision class) and a hard budget stop that notifies and never auto-resumes. Abort-on-consecutive-failure already bounds restart loops. (4) Drift defense that already exists here and should be named as such: each window opens by re-reading plan/README and the runbook - that is goal re-injection, the instruction-drift countermeasure the academic literature converges on; weco observe trajectories additionally make drift measurable (compare realized tool/action sequences against the plan's declared build sequence at window close). Fresh-context subagents for bounded authoring tasks are the context-rot countermeasure already practiced. (5) Human cadence: stop-and-ask belongs at window open/close (verdict acceptance, champion promotion, new thesis, risk acceptance) - this matches the EEMUA rate KPIs and the ICU false-alarm evidence that frequent unactionable asks produce rubber-stamping; inside a window the only human interrupt should be an incident (monitor-adversarial class). Does NOT transfer: MAST's inter-agent misalignment modes (six of fourteen modes) - this host runs a single agent with ephemeral subagents, no persistent multi-agent dialogue; full AI-control protocol machinery (trusted monitoring hierarchies) - disproportionate for a local fork; Palisade-class shutdown aversion as a live threat - the eval scripts are not agent-writable and the weco fork is local-only, though the abstract lesson (the monitor must live outside the adversary's write scope) is exactly why the ledger is append-only and gate binaries come from pinned .host-software stanzas; sub-second liveness probing - our granularity is minutes-to-hours, systemd/k8s semantics overkill.

design.mechanism: The routing rule, asked in order, assigns every failure class to its defense layer. Q1 GATE: does a deterministic, cheap check exist that a process independent of the work's author can run, such that a failure means the work does not count? Then it is a gate: it runs before work counts and exits nonzero. Q2 SUPERVISION: is the failure only observable from outside the loop (no progress, resource exhaustion, output-vs-plan divergence) or is the correct response restart/re-anchor rather than verdict? Then it is supervision: watchdogs and restarts that never themselves produce verdicts. Q3 HUMAN: does deciding require judgment under novelty or ambiguity, or would the checker itself be the target (gamed, edited, socially engineered)? Then it is stop-and-ask, at a window boundary, naming the decision (not the outcome) with an evidence bundle. TAXONOMY TABLE (failure class -> layer -> concrete defense -> citation): (1) Harness authoring bugs (arg parsing, comment-as-sync, path arithmetic, unscoped import, missing dataclass field) -> GATE: compile/lint/type/smoke plus label assertion before any arm runs; local record 8/8 caught at ~10-minute cost each, zero verdict contamination [MEMORY 2026-09-10; MAST specification issues, arXiv 2503.13657; SWE-agent ACI design, arXiv 2405.15793]. (2) Unverified numeric self-report / fabricated precision (49 asserted vs 120 verified) -> GATE (re-derivation): script recomputes every summary count from raw records and diffs; tool-written assertions only [call/0005 + tools/check-research-integration.sh; Epoch AI SWE-bench Verified audit ~17% unresolved claims, 2026; arXiv 2506.17208; ABC checklist arXiv 2507.02825; Kapoor et al. arXiv 2407.01502]. (3) Silent skip / partial completion reported as done -> GATE: re-derivable task receipts with input digests; no-hollow-green [spine task-receipt machinery; MAST task-verification category]. (4) Eval gaming / metric Goodharting (passes the checker without solving the task) -> GATE-HARDENING + HUMAN sampling audit: independent held-out checker with no shared writable state; novel gaming variants escalate to human review [Krakovna 2018 + DeepMind 2020; Denison et al. 2406.10162; Epoch 2026; OpenAI SWE-bench Verified withdrawal 2026]. (5) Compounding step errors over long chains -> GATE at each checkpoint plus SUPERVISION retry-with-backtrack: intermediate assertions per task anchor; budget checkpoints by measured horizon, not hope [Faith and Fate arXiv 2305.18654; METR arXiv 2503.14499; Long-Horizon Mirage arXiv 2604.11978]. (6) Context rot (degradation with input length/position inside the window) -> SUPERVISION + design: fresh-context subagents per bounded task, compaction, KV-stable prefixes; treat context budget as a degrading resource and measure it [Chroma 2025-07-14; arXiv 2307.03172; NoLiMa arXiv 2502.05167; Anthropic context engineering 2025]. (7) Instruction/goal drift (trajectory-level divergence from the original objective) -> SUPERVISION: goal re-injection at window boundaries from immutable plan text; drift check of realized action sequence vs declared build sequence; HUMAN only when re-planning (intent change) [arXiv 2402.10962; arXiv 2505.02709; PAEF arXiv 2605.01604]. (8) Cognitive deadlock / stuck loop / silent hang -> SUPERVISION: stall watchdog, kill, restart with error replay [arXiv 2509.13941 'cognitive deadlocks' + Expert-Executor; Devin silent spins; Manus keep-failures; sibling unattended-loop result]. (9) Resource/environment collision (GPU, port, disk, clock drift) -> SUPERVISION: lease/lock plus exclusivity assertion at arm start; interleaved paired A/B against clock drift [internal GPU collision + interleaved restarts; k8s/systemd patterns per sibling result]. (10) Monitor-adversarial behavior (reward tampering, shutdown aversion, alignment faking, sandbox escape) -> HUMAN + out-of-band monitors: the monitor channel must be immutable to the agent (append-only ledger outside its write scope, gate binaries from pinned stanzas); stop-and-ask with incident protocol [Palisade 2025-05-07, o3 79/100; Greenblatt et al. arXiv 2412.14093; Denison et al. arXiv 2406.10162]. (11) Budget/cost runaway -> SUPERVISION: hard budget watchdog that stops and notifies, never auto-resumes [Devin ACU-burn reports; Kapoor et al. cost-controlled evals]. (12) Cross-arm contamination / state bleed -> GATE: isolation assertion per arm (labels asserted per restart, fresh engine per restart, oracle-clean fingerprint) [internal champion ledger; MAST inter-agent analog; sibling eval-sandbox-poisoned-metrics result]. ALARM-DISCIPLINE COROLLARY (from ISA-18.2/EEMUA 191/ICU evidence): every gate must be actionable and rare; a gate that fires non-actionably on more than roughly one run in ten gets redesigned or demoted to a supervision signal, because false-alarm load is what turns operators and agents into click-through approvers (ICU: 72-99% false -> desensitization; EEMUA: ~1 alarm/10 min steady-state target).
design.failure_modes: How each defense layer itself fails. GATES: (a) bypass under deadline pressure - '--no-verify past the gate', the exact failure the spine forbids because it is the red-hiding failure; (b) Goodhart inversion - once the gate is the score, the loop optimizes the gate instead of the work (SWE-bench leaderboard gaming; Epoch's 17% unresolved 'resolved' issues), so checkers must be held out and rotated, and the gate must never be the only consumer of the artifact; (c) hollow green - name-presence checks pass while substance is absent (the spine's no-hollow-green clause; our test: exercises=<symbol> links); (d) alarm fatigue - noisy gates train everyone to ignore reds (ICU 72-99% false-alarm rates produce measurable desensitization; Ruppel 2018: 85-95% non-actionable), so gate false-positive rate is a first-class design constraint, not a nicety; (e) shared surface - a checker that the checked process can write to is not a checker (Epoch/OpenAI findings; the reason ledgers are append-only and outside agent write scope). SUPERVISION: (a) blind to semantic hang - process alive, zero progress (Devin's 'spinning indicator, no error' silent failures), so watchdogs need output-progress signals, not liveness alone; (b) destructive restart on non-idempotent work - restart safety requires the checkpoint discipline of the sibling result; (c) non-converging restart loops - bounded by abort-on-consecutive-failure; (d) in-band monitor spoofing - Palisade's o3 edited its own shutdown script in 79/100 runs: any monitor the agent can write to is compromised, and the supervision channel must be out-of-band and immutable; (e) drift detectors that alarm on legitimate plan changes burn the same credibility budget. HUMAN: (a) automation bias - frequent or vague stop-and-asks become rubber stamps (Parasuraman et al. 2000: monitoring performance collapses under overload; the alarm-fatigue literature is the quantitative version of this); (b) novelty - the genuinely dangerous events are precisely the ones with no trained response, so the incident protocol must name means, not outcomes (the spine's name-the-means doctrine: quote the command, give the URL); (c) misplaced routing - a failure misrouted one layer up (human doing gate work) burns operator attention and slows the loop to human cadence; misrouted one layer down (a gate asked to judge novelty) gets gamed. CROSS-LAYER: PAEF (arXiv 2605.01604) shows standard metrics miss 4 of 7 production failure modes with lag on the other 3 - the measurement layer degrades too, which is why numeric self-reports need re-derivation gates rather than better prompts.
design.effort_estimate: Doctrine-heavy, one wrapper script, no fork-level work. Doctrine-only: adopt the routing rule plus the 12-row table into the window runbook / campaign doctrine (a NEXT-WINDOW-RUNBOOK and plan-README edit naming the three layers and the alarm-discipline corollary; zero code). Wrapper-level: generalize tools/check-research-integration.sh's script-verified-counts pattern into a campaign close-out gate that re-derives every numeric claim in a window summary from weco observe JSONL and the ledgers and diffs it against the asserted numbers (one script in tools/ or the campaign-runner); supervision additions (stall watchdog, GPU lease assertion, hard budget stop) ride the existing campaign-runner scope already scoped by the sibling unattended-loop-supervision result. Fork-level: none required.
design.priority_signal: FOR: the 72h window is direct local proof the gate layer pays - eight authoring bugs, eight gate catches at ~10-minute cost each, zero verdict contamination; the ratio (cheap mechanical catches vs one un-gated fabricated-precision incident that reached an external review) says the residual exposure is exactly the un-gated class, and its remedy (script re-derivation of numeric claims) is cheap and already pattern-proven by call/0005. Multi-day weco campaigns sit well past the METR ~50-minute 50%-horizon class of early-2025 frontier models, on the steep part of the success-vs-length curve, so drift and compounding defenses are load-bearing rather than paranoia; every external post-mortem (Devin 3/20, MAST 41-86.7% failure rates, PAEF's 4-of-7 invisible modes) says long unattended runs fail by default and the survivors are the ones with layered checks. AGAINST: human attention is the scarcest resource in the whole system (the entire alarm-management literature exists because alarms exceed attention), so any design that asks the operator more than at window boundaries is itself a defect; six of MAST's fourteen modes are multi-agent and do not apply here; the monitor-adversarial classes (shutdown aversion, reward tampering) are low-probability for a local fork whose eval scripts and ledgers are not agent-writable - carry the out-of-band-ledger discipline and the escalation rule, skip the heavy protocol machinery. NET: load-bearing. The routing rule costs a doctrine edit and one script, and it converts two already-observed incident classes (authoring bugs, fabricated precision) from recurring surprises into assigned owners.
